headline: Diplomacy is pulling some of the oil premium out going into Fed week. Brent is down ≈1.9% to ≈$114.5 as Qatari, Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani envoys work Tehran, the 10Y is back under 5% at ≈4.97% and S&P futures are up ≈0.2%. A December hike is still ≈79% priced going into today's $69B 2Y auction.
summary: Oil: the weekend's Houthi claims on Yanbu and Rabigh did not produce a Sunday-night spike. CNBC has Brent down 1.89% to $114.51 (Fri settle $116.72) and WTI down $2.23 to ≈$101.04. Qatari mediators reached Tehran on Sunday, and Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iranian officials today. Trump says it is 'getting to be decision time' between a deal and renewed strikes, Iran's parliament says talks are pointless until its seven conditions are met, and the NYT's post-midterm (Nov 3) strike-planning report still stands.

Rates: the 10Y is ≈4.97–4.98%, down ≈1–2 bp, after closing Friday at ≈5.00%. The 2Y is ≈4.675% and the 30Y ≈5.30%, near one-month lows. The $69B 2Y auction (12:00 PM CT) is the first read on front-end demand before Wednesday's decision. The last 2Y cleared at 4.787%, so this one should clear ≈11 bp lower, and a tail would mean buyers want more yield to hold hike risk.

Fed: CME FedWatch shows ≈91% for a hold at 3.75–4.00% on Wed Oct 28 (1:00 PM CT, Warsh presser 1:30 PM) and ≈78–80% for a December hike. There is no SEP, so the statement and presser carry the signal. TD Securities expects a hold now and hikes in December and March, but says the chance of a surprise hike is 'higher than normal.' GDP and PCE follow Thursday at 7:30 AM CT.

Europe: France avoided a downgrade. Moody's affirmed Aa3 with a negative outlook, and the OAT–Bund 10Y spread has narrowed to ≈158–161 bp from Friday's ≈176 bp peak (it widened ≈29 bp last week, per Saxo). The CAC leads European gains. The ECB (Thu), BoJ (Fri) and BoC (Wed) also decide this week, so it is a full central-bank week.

Deals: EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal (0.987 EQT per Range share) at a pro forma enterprise value above $50B, creating the largest U.S. integrated natural-gas producer, with $325M of synergies rising to more than $600M. Ovintiv is buying Montney producer Logan Energy for ≈C$1.26B in cash. That is fee flow for energy coverage and leveraged finance desks, alongside SpaceX's reported $40B Apollo-led debt package for Nvidia chips.

Metals: gold is stuck at ≈$4,000 (quotes $3,986–4,015) after a ≈4% weekly loss and its first sub-$4,000 print since mid-July. Oil is feeding December hike odds and real yields, which outweighs the haven bid. Silver is ≈$54.0 (down ≈11% over the month). On the LME, copper is down 0.56% at $14,242.50/t as warehouse stocks build, even though China's Yangshan premium sits at multi-year highs.
markets_asof: Post-open ≈9:15 AM CT. Index levels are early-session snapshots (Yahoo Finance and TheStreet), yields come from Trading Economics, and oil and metals are spot or front-month quotes that vary by source.

calendar.event: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iranian officials in Tehran (Qatari mediators arrived Sun)
calendar.why: This is the main driver of oil's ≈2% drop overnight. A credible step toward a deal would pull more premium out of crude and December hike odds. A collapse, or a confirmed hit at Yanbu, would reverse it quickly.
Verizon's 8-K cites its best Q3 postpaid phone net adds in five years, lower churn and a third straight guidance raise. It is a defensive, high-dividend name (70.75¢ quarterly) in a 5% 10Y world.
The Chicago Fed's broad 85-indicator growth gauge. A reading below zero supports the growth-scare side of last week's bond rally, but it rarely moves markets by itself.
Texas factories are an oil-patch read. Watch the prices-paid component for evidence that $100+ crude is feeding through to input costs.
Treasury is buying back illiquid long bonds. That modestly supports the long end, where term premium has been pushing 30Y yields above 5.3%.

This is the cleanest pre-FOMC test of demand for front-end paper with a December hike ≈79% priced. A tail means dealers had to absorb more of the supply, while a stop-through says buyers think hike pricing has peaked.

calendar.event: Earnings: Amkor, Alexandria Real Estate, Welltower
calendar.why: Amkor is an AI chip-packaging read before MSFT and GOOGL Wednesday. Alexandria tests life-science office credit.

calendar.event: Boeing Q3 (pre-mkt, call 9:30 AM CT); Conference Board confidence 9:00 AM; 5Y auction ($70B) 12:00 PM
calendar.why: Options imply about a ±6.5% Boeing move. Confidence is at 2014-type lows. The 5Y is the most Fed-sensitive point on the curve, one day before the decision.

calendar.consensus: Hold 2.25% favored (hike odds ≈16–33% in prediction markets)
calendar.why: Sources disagree. Canada shed 68K jobs in September, but headline CPI is 3.1%, so the decision shows how central banks are weighing an oil shock against weak labor markets.

calendar.event: FOMC decision (Warsh presser 1:30 PM); 2Y FRN auction
calendar.why: This is the next FOMC. With no SEP, any hint that December is live (≈79% priced) or off the table moves the 2Y, SOFR Dec/Mar spreads and gold.

calendar.event: Q3 GDP (advance) + Sep PCE; 8:15 AM ECB decision
calendar.consensus: GDP ≈3.0%; core PCE 3.1% y/y; ECB hold 2.50%
calendar.why: This marks the Fed's message to data within 18 hours. Markets price ≈75% for a December ECB hike, so Lagarde's tone matters for Bunds and the OAT spread.
The 10Y JGB is ≈2.78%, and a hawkish BoJ would add to global term premium. The oil majors will show how much of $100+ crude reaches buybacks.

rates.title: Yields slip back under 5% as oil eases
rates.body: The 10Y is ≈4.97–4.98% (≈−1 to −2 bp) and the 30Y ≈5.30%, near one-month lows, after Friday's close at ≈5.001%. The 2Y is ≈4.675%, barely changed. The move follows Brent's ≈2% drop on Qatari mediation, and the $69B 2Y auction should clear ≈11 bp below September's 4.787%.
rates.simple: A Treasury yield is the interest the U.S. government pays to borrow. It falls when bond prices rise. Cheaper oil means less inflation pressure, so investors bought bonds and yields dipped. That feeds directly into mortgage and corporate borrowing costs.

rates.title: Fed: a hold ≈91% priced, December ≈79%
rates.body: CME FedWatch shows ≈90.6–91% for a hold at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28 and ≈78–80% for a 25 bp December hike. TD Securities sees hikes in December and March and says the risk of a surprise hike this week is 'higher than normal.' There are no new projections, so the statement language and the Warsh presser carry the signal.
rates.simple: The Fed sets the overnight rate that anchors all other interest rates. Traders are nearly certain it holds this week but mostly expect another increase in December because oil is keeping inflation high. Anything Warsh says on Wednesday that moves those December odds will reprice short-term borrowing costs right away.
rates.source: FXStreet (CME FedWatch); TD Securities via FXStreet

rates.title: France avoids a downgrade and the OAT–Bund spread snaps tighter
rates.body: Moody's affirmed France at Aa3 with a negative outlook. The 10Y OAT–Bund spread has narrowed to ≈158–161 bp from ≈176 bp on Friday, after widening ≈29 bp last week; on Oct 23 the OAT was ≈5.05% vs the Bund's ≈3.33%. The ECB is expected to hold at 2.50% Thursday, with headline inflation at 3.8%.
rates.simple: The spread is the extra yield investors demand to lend to France instead of Germany, and it is a fear gauge for French debt. A rating agency declining to downgrade calmed nerves for now, but a negative outlook means a cut is still possible. Wider European spreads can pull U.S. yields and bank funding costs up with them.

derivatives.title: Brent curve: a ≈$15 backwardation says the shock looks temporary
derivatives.body: Dec Brent is ≈$114.5, the Jan '27 contract is down ≈1.6% this morning, and the April 2027 contract trades just under $100. That puts roughly $15 of backwardation into the front five months. Dec Brent expires this week, so roll flows add noise to front-month moves.
derivatives.simple: Backwardation means oil for delivery soon costs more than oil for delivery later. Traders are paying up for barrels now because of the Middle East risk but expect prices to ease. That shape rewards holding physical oil and is why producers hedge, or lock in, future prices.

derivatives.title: CME: October is tracking a record, and SOFR options are surging
derivatives.body: CME says October ADV is tracking its highest October on record, after a record September of 31.8M contracts/day (+22% y/y), rates ADV of 16.2M (+22%) and Treasury futures and options ADV of 9.5M (+42%). Treasury futures OI is ≈24M. SOFR options traded ≈1.6M/day, +41% m/m.
derivatives.simple: ADV (average daily volume) counts how many futures and options contracts trade each day, and open interest (OI) counts how many positions stay open. Records mean investors are paying to hedge interest-rate risk around an unusually uncertain Fed. That turns into exchange fee revenue for Chicago-based CME.

derivatives.title: Fed-week positioning: express it through Dec/Mar SOFR, not the outright
derivatives.body: With ≈79% priced for December and TD flagging above-normal surprise risk for Wednesday, the asymmetric trades sit in short-dated SOFR options and the Dec/Mar SOFR futures spread. Treasury vol (MOVE) closed last week near ≈99. The Thursday GDP and PCE data add a second event inside the same option expiry window.
derivatives.simple: SOFR futures let traders bet on where overnight rates will be in future months. Options on them pay off if rates move sharply. When the Fed is close to a coin-flip on its next move, buying that protection is cheaper than taking a big one-way bet.

metals.title: Gold pinned at $4,000 by the oil-to-hike channel
metals.body: Gold lost ≈4% last week and printed below $4,000 for the first time since mid-July (≈$3,998 Friday). Monday quotes run from $3,986 to $4,015. It sits ≈29% below its ≈$5,590 record, with $3,943 flagged as the next support. CIBC cut its forecasts but sees $5,200 in 2027, and central banks bought a net 39t in August (WGC).
metals.simple: Gold pays no interest, so it struggles when inflation-adjusted (real) yields and expected Fed rates rise. Expensive oil is pushing up Fed hike bets and hurting gold even as war risk would normally help it. Steady central-bank buying is the main floor under the price.

metals.title: Silver and PGMs: underperforming gold on the way down
metals.body: Silver is ≈$54.0 (+0.2% vs Friday's $53.92) but down ≈11% over the past month. Platinum is ≈$1,547 and palladium ≈$1,043, down from ≈$1,717 and ≈$1,207 at the end of September. These high-beta metals fall harder than gold when growth fears and the dollar both bite.
metals.simple: Silver, platinum and palladium are part precious metal and part industrial input for solar panels, car catalysts and electronics. When investors worry about slower growth they get hit twice, so they swing more than gold. That makes them a fast read on risk appetite.

metals.title: Copper: LME stocks build while China's premium screams tight
metals.body: LME 3M copper is down 0.56% at $14,242.50/t, still near the $14,875 record from Sep 11, while COMEX is ≈$6.46/lb. China's September imports rose 20.7% m/m to 461kt, the Yangshan premium is $148–168/t (multi-year highs, by source) and Shanghai-monitored stocks fell more than 25% to 54,356t. LME Week speakers warned that AI data-center demand forecasts are being revised down.
metals.simple: Copper goes into wiring, power grids and data centers, so its price reflects global building and electrification. Rising warehouse stocks in London suggest enough supply for now, but Chinese buyers are paying record premiums to import it. Those two signals point in opposite directions, and that keeps prices volatile.

banking.title: EQT buys Range Resources: a $50B+ all-stock gas megadeal
banking.body: Range holders get 0.987 EQT shares each, for a pro forma enterprise value above $50B and a 73%/27% ownership split. EQT targets $325M of annual synergies within two years and more than $600M longer term, expands its board to 12 and expects to close in Q1 2027. Separately, Ovintiv is buying Montney oil producer Logan Energy for ≈C$1.26B (≈$890M) in cash.
banking.simple: An all-stock deal means EQT pays with its own shares rather than cash, so Range's owners become EQT owners. Merging two Appalachian gas producers is meant to cut costs and supply growing gas demand from power plants and data centers. Megadeals like this generate large advisory and financing fees for investment banks.

banking.title: SpaceX's $40B chip financing tests IG demand
banking.body: The package reportedly splits into ≈$10B of bank loans and ≈$30B of investment-grade bonds, with Apollo leading and Pimco among the lenders, to fund a Nvidia GPU order. Nvidia is both the supplier and a SpaceX shareholder (≈122.8M shares). CNBC reports Musk said the financing has closed.
banking.simple: Investment-grade (IG) bonds are debt from borrowers judged safe enough for conservative investors like pension funds. A $30B bond from a single company competes with a wave of other AI-related borrowing, which can push credit spreads (extra yield over Treasuries) wider for everyone. Banks earn fees but also take on loan exposure to the AI buildout.

banking.title: Northern Trust Q3: core EPS +40% y/y; Wintrust buys a guardianship unit
banking.body: Northern Trust earned $642.9M, or $3.40 a share, vs $2.29 a year ago (Q2 was $4.23 including a Visa exchange gain). Excluding notable items, revenue rose 11%, pretax income 21% and EPS 40% y/y. Wintrust ($72B in assets, the No. 3 bank in Chicago) is buying NT's ≈$1.2B-AUM guardianship business.
banking.simple: Northern Trust is a Chicago custody and wealth bank that earns fees for holding and managing assets, plus interest on deposits. Higher markets and rates lifted both income streams. Wintrust's purchase shows regional banks adding fee businesses to reduce their reliance on lending.

banking.title: Healthcare and real estate M&A: Surgery Partners, Ingenia
banking.body: The FT reports Bon Secours Mercy Health is in late-stage talks to buy a majority stake in Surgery Partners at ≈$6B including debt. The WSJ digest says Australia's Ingenia Communities cut Warburg Pincus off from its data room after a rival $1.55B bid from AVID Property Group.
banking.simple: A data room is where bidders review a company's confidential financials before making an offer. Locking out one bidder signals the seller prefers a rival offer. Both deals show private capital and strategic buyers are still active even with 5% long-term rates.
banking.source: CNBC (FT); Reuters WSJ digest via Boursorama

cnbc.title: Treasury yields inch lower before the Fed decision
cnbc.body: The 10Y fell less than 1 bp to ≈4.98%, the 30Y 1 bp to 5.302% and the 2Y was ≈flat at 4.6752%. Traders put >90% odds on a hold at 3.75–4.00%, with PCE due Thursday.
cnbc.simple: Bond yields barely moved because investors are waiting for the Fed on Wednesday. Small moves before a big event are normal. Traders don't want large positions until they hear the chair.

cnbc.title: Oil falls as diplomacy picks up
cnbc.body: Brent fell 1.89% to $114.51 from Friday's $116.72 settle, its highest since April, after Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran. The weekend's Houthi strike claims on Saudi targets remain unconfirmed.
cnbc.simple: Oil prices carry a 'risk premium', an extra amount for the chance that supply gets cut off. Signs of peace talks shrink that premium. Gasoline and inflation expectations follow.

cnbc.title: Busiest week of earnings meets the Fed
cnbc.body: CNBC's Investing Club flags the peak week of Q3 reporting (MSFT and GOOGL Wed, AMZN Thu, XOM and CVX Fri) colliding with the two-day FOMC that ends Wednesday.
cnbc.simple: This week, many of the largest U.S. companies report profits at the same time the Fed sets rates. Either one could move the whole market. Together they make volatile days more likely.

cnbc.title: Surgery Partners in talks; SpaceX's $40B debt closes
cnbc.body: CNBC's live blog cites the FT on Bon Secours Mercy's late-stage talks for a majority stake in Surgery Partners (≈$6B with debt), and Musk saying SpaceX's $40B Nvidia-chip debt raise has closed.
cnbc.simple: These are two big financings in a week of market stress. Lenders and buyers are still writing large checks. That keeps bank deal pipelines full.

wsj.title: Ingenia shuts Warburg Pincus out after a rival $1.55B bid
wsj.body: Per the Reuters digest of the WSJ, Australia's Ingenia Communities revoked Warburg Pincus's data-room access after receiving a competing $1.55B offer from AVID Property Group.
wsj.simple: In a sale, bidders get access to a private 'data room' of company information. Cutting one off suggests the board is leaning toward the other offer. Bidding wars usually raise the price shareholders get.

wsj.title: Roche's lung-cancer drug cuts death risk 44%
wsj.body: The WSJ digest reports Roche's experimental divarasib cut the risk of death by 44% vs existing treatments in a Phase III trial.
wsj.simple: A Phase III trial is the final large test before a drug can be approved. A 44% reduction in death risk is a big result. It could become a major revenue source and spur pharma deal activity.

wsj.title: AstraZeneca prepares a filing for a new targeted cancer drug line
wsj.body: The same digest says AstraZeneca is preparing a regulatory filing for the first in a new family of targeted cancer drugs, as both companies present at ESMO.
wsj.simple: Drug makers file with regulators like the FDA to get permission to sell. Being first with a new type of treatment can lock in market share for years. That matters for healthcare equity and credit investors.
wsj.source: Reuters WSJ digest via Boursorama; MarketScreener

tribune.title: CME: record October volume tracking, CFO handoff Nov 2
tribune.body: CME says October ADV is tracking its best October ever, after a record Q3 and September ADV of 31.8M (+22%). Jack Tobin takes over as CFO on Nov 2.
tribune.simple: CME, headquartered in Chicago, makes money each time a futures contract trades. Fed and oil uncertainty means record trading. That flows straight to its earnings.

tribune.title: Northern Trust's strong quarter; Wintrust adds a trust unit
tribune.body: Northern Trust's adjusted EPS rose 40% y/y in Q3 ($3.40 reported). Wintrust, the No. 3 bank in Chicago, is buying NT's $1.2B guardianship business.
tribune.simple: Two of Chicago's biggest banks are growing their fee businesses. Fees from managing money are steadier than loan income. They hold up even when rates swing.

tribune.title: Chicago Fed activity index lands this morning
tribune.body: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for September is due at 7:30 AM CT, with consensus at −0.10 vs −0.04 prior.
tribune.simple: This index combines 85 economic indicators into one number, where zero means the economy is growing at its normal pace. A negative reading means slightly below-trend growth. It is one input into whether the Fed keeps hiking.

tribune.title: Chicago's Formic raises $50M for factory robots
tribune.body: Chicago robot-rental startup Formic raised a $50M Series B (Oct 23) to move into general-purpose machines for U.S. factories.
tribune.simple: Formic rents robots to manufacturers instead of selling them, which lowers the upfront cost. Venture money still flows to Chicago industrial tech. That is a growth area for local commercial bankers.

nyt.title: U.S. and Israel plan post-midterm Iran strikes; target list reportedly widened
nyt.body: The NYT reported Oct 22 that the U.S. and Israel have plans for renewed strikes after the Nov 3 midterms. A secondhand Oct 26 summary says the target list now includes Iranian energy and economic infrastructure, and that Iran warned U.S. diplomats could be targets.
nyt.simple: This is why oil still carries a big risk premium despite peace talks. Strikes on energy sites would threaten supply directly. Markets treat early November as the danger window.
nyt.source: NYT via Times of Israel; newsletter summary

nyt.title: Trump: 'decision time' on Iran
nyt.body: Trump said it is 'getting to be decision time' on a deal vs renewed attacks, while U.S. officials say reports that a deal is close are wrong. Iran's ambassador to Pakistan offered to reopen Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its naval blockade.
nyt.simple: Both sides are bargaining in public. A Hormuz reopening would be the biggest bearish oil event possible because about a fifth of world oil normally passes through it. Failure would push prices back up.
nyt.source: Newsquawk; Iran International (NYT digest not found)

talking_points.topic: Reading today's 2Y auction as a Fed-week signal
talking_points.point: The last 2Y cleared at 4.787%, and today's $69B should come ≈11 bp lower near 4.67%, with a December hike ≈79% priced and a hold ≈91%. A tail would mean dealers had to absorb the supply because end-buyers don't believe hike pricing has peaked. A stop-through says the front end is already well hedged. Follow it with tomorrow's 5Y, then Warsh: three readings on the same question within 48 hours.

talking_points.topic: Brent backwardation and what it says about inflation
talking_points.point: Brent is ≈$114.5 at the front and just under $100 for April 2027, roughly $15 of backwardation. The futures market treats the Iran and Houthi shock as temporary. That is why breakevens and 10Y yields haven't fully tracked spot crude, and why the Fed can argue over headline vs core. For a derivatives desk, steep backwardation lifts producer hedging demand and the roll yield for long holders, and it shifts the risk to the shape of the curve, not just the price.

talking_points.topic: Gold at $4,000 is trading rates, not war
talking_points.point: Gold fell ≈4% in a week that had Houthi strikes and Iran war talk, because oil raised December hike odds and real yields. The haven bid lost to the cost of holding a metal that pays no interest. The floor is official-sector buying (39t net in August per WGC; Goldman's 50t/month base case) and CIBC's $5,200 call for 2027. If Warsh opens the door to skipping December, gold is the cleanest beneficiary. If he leans hawkish, $3,943 is the next level.

caveats: Direct page fetches failed this run (DNS errors), so every figure comes from search excerpts. Pre-market levels for futures, yields, oil, gold and DXY are early-session snapshots that differ by source (gold $3,986–4,015). Dow and Russell show Friday's cash close because no futures level was found. No WSJ or NYT originals were reachable: WSJ items come from a machine-translated Reuters digest, and the NYT bucket uses secondhand reports (the Oct 22 strike-planning story plus an unverified Oct 26 summary). The Tribune bucket uses CME, SEC, Crain's and The Next Web. BoC odds conflict across sources. The Surgery Partners and SpaceX items come from CNBC's Oct 25 page citing the FT and Musk. The 10Y TIPS level wasn't reliably dated and is omitted.

updates.label: Post-open
updates.headline: Stocks opened higher and the oil premium kept leaking after Trump said there would be no strike 'today'. Gold is back above $4,000 and the 10Y is holding just under 5% ahead of the noon $69B 2Y auction.
points: Open: S&P 500 ≈7,660 (≈+0.5%), Dow ≈52,450–52,490 (≈+0.4–0.5%), Nasdaq ≈+0.2–0.3% (Yahoo Finance and TheStreet, ≈9:10 AM CT). The Dow is coming off its third straight weekly gain, and the S&P lost 0.5% last week.

Iran: Trump told reporters on Sunday that 'there will not be a strike today', but reports say the Pentagon is still planning possible post-midterm strikes. WTI is holding ≈$101. Kitco and FXStreet have Brent easing toward ≈$114, while one Investing.com feed shows ≈$110 (possibly a different contract month), so treat oil levels as approximate.

Rates: the 10Y is ≈4.97–4.99% and the 2Y ≈4.67%, little changed from pre-market, with the $69B 2Y auction at 12:00 PM CT (last 4.787%). Trading Economics prices ≈10% for a hike Wednesday and ≈80% for December, while Mitrade cites ≈69% for December, so sources now disagree more than this morning's 78–80%.

Metals: Kitco has spot gold at ≈$4,014 (+0.5%) in early U.S. trade, which reverses Friday's $3,975 low (weakest since Jul 20). It credits lower oil easing Fed-tightening fears. Silver is ≈$54 and COMEX copper ≈$6.49/lb, both little changed.

Data and earnings: we couldn't find the September CFNAI result (7:30 AM). The Dallas Fed survey is due at 9:30 AM, so the morning brief's consensus stands. Verizon reported before the open and its 8-K confirms the guidance raise, but we haven't seen a clean read on the stock's move. No new bank M&A so far.
updates.simple: An oil-price 'war premium' is the extra amount traders pay for oil because they fear a supply disruption. When the U.S. president said no attack would happen today, some of that premium came out of oil, and stocks rose because cheaper energy means less inflation pressure. Less inflation pressure makes it less likely the Fed has to raise interest rates. Gold gained for the same reason: fewer expected rate hikes make a metal that pays no interest more attractive to own.
